clinicalPearls: A congenital abnormality in which scalp hair is tightly curled, fine and often lighter in colour in individuals not of African descent, present from infancy
It occurs as a diffuse hereditary form with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance, or as a localised woolly hair naevus consisting of a well-circumscribed patch of abnormal hair

The recessive forms carry important cardiocutaneous associations, namely Naxos disease (woolly hair, palmoplantar keratoderma and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy) and Carvajal syndrome (woolly hair, palmoplantar keratoderma and a dilated, left-dominant cardiomyopathy)
These desmosomal-gene disorders carry a risk of life-threatening arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death, so woolly hair with palmoplantar keratoderma should prompt cardiac evaluation
The hair is frequently sparse and slow-growing and may show associated shaft abnormalities such as pili torti or trichorrhexis nodosa
Diagnosis is clinical with microscopy of the shaft, and the key step is screening for associated keratoderma and cardiomyopathy in suspected syndromic cases
Management is supportive for the hair itself, with the priority being cardiac surveillance and genetic counselling in syndromic forms
reference.pathophysiology: Woolly hair reflects an abnormal, tightly coiled hair shaft with an altered elliptical cross-section and often reduced diameter, present from birth in non-African scalp hair. Hereditary diffuse forms and the localised naevus arise from defects in hair-shaft formation. The clinically critical recessive syndromes, Naxos disease and Carvajal syndrome, result from mutations in desmosomal genes encoding plakoglobin and desmoplakin, which impair cell-to-cell adhesion in the epidermis, hair and myocardium and thereby explain the triad of woolly hair, palmoplantar keratoderma and cardiomyopathy with arrhythmogenic risk.
additionalDifferentials: Normal tightly curled or afro-textured hair
Pili torti, with a twisted shaft
Trichorrhexis nodosa and other fragility disorders
Acquired progressive kinking of the hair
additionalInvestigations: Light microscopy of the shaft to characterise the curl and detect associated defects
Examination of the palms and soles for palmoplantar keratoderma
Electrocardiography and echocardiography where a cardiocutaneous syndrome is suspected
Genetic testing for desmosomal-gene mutations such as JUP and DSP, with family screening
Cardiology referral and a family history of sudden cardiac death
redFlags: Woolly hair with palmoplantar keratoderma, mandating cardiac assessment for Naxos or Carvajal syndrome
Palpitations, syncope or a family history of sudden cardiac death
Any features of arrhythmogenic or dilated cardiomyopathy
reference.prognosis: Isolated woolly hair and the woolly hair naevus are benign and tend to improve in later childhood or adult life, but the outlook in Naxos and Carvajal syndromes is dominated by the cardiomyopathy and its arrhythmic risk, making early cardiac diagnosis potentially life-saving.
pitfalls: Regarding woolly hair as a purely cosmetic issue and missing an associated life-threatening cardiomyopathy
Failing to examine the palms and soles for keratoderma
Not taking a family history of sudden cardiac death
Overlooking associated hair-shaft defects on microscopy
management: Screen for the cardiocutaneous syndromes by examining palms and soles for palmoplantar keratoderma and arranging cardiac assessment when present
Cardiac management of associated cardiomyopathy in Naxos and Carvajal syndromes, including heart failure therapy and an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator for arrhythmogenic and sudden-death risk
Emollients and keratolytics for palmoplantar keratoderma
Gentle hair care, since isolated woolly hair and the woolly hair naevus are benign and need no specific hair treatment, with reassurance that they often improve with age
Genetic testing for desmosomal genes such as JUP and DSP with cascade cardiac and genetic screening of relatives
Cardiology referral and documentation of any family history of sudden cardiac death
Urgent escalation for palpitations, syncope or documented arrhythmia in syndromic cases
